name: Natco Pharma
why: Management outlook: I think this year, we expect that domestic will increase by about 25% in volumes alone.
Domestic institutions (mutual funds, insurers) raised holding by 5.4 pts in a year
Profits backed by cash: operating cash flow is 100% of 3-year profit
Sector cycle: Earnings improving but price not confirming
risks: Not at record: quarterly sales, quarterly profit, annual sales, annual profit
Margins shrinking (42% to 27%) - record profit may be near peak
Working capital stretching - debtor days 103 to 79, inventory days 405 to 480 (rising): check receivables / stock build-up
Latest quarter Sep 2026: Weak (sales -29% YoY, profit -61% YoY)

Cost quality weak: margin shrinking or operating profit falling (costs 58% to 73% of sales)

guidance: I think this year, we expect that domestic will increase by about 25% in volumes alone.
We expect Q2 to be significantly better than Q1, and I think we are on track to, again, as I said, to break even for the year.
capex: Amit Parekh: Organically, I think every year, we have around INR250 crores to INR300 crores of capex year- on-year.
risks: As probably most of you are aware, there has been the El Nino fear and delay in rains.
So that is what actually caused a little bit of delay in the cropping season.
focus: I think I would focus on the larger picture.

gates.t: Company is growing: latest quarter profit -61% and sales -29% year on year
Long-run growth: profit -16% a year over 3 years
Promoters raising their stake or insiders buying (promoter holding 46.2%, -3.3 pts in a year)
Nobody selling: promoters not reducing, no pledged shares, no insider selling
Price in an uptrend (above its 200-day average)

Working capital healthy (debtor and inventory days not rising)

about: NATCO Pharma Limited (NATCO) is a vertically integrated, research and development focused pharmaceutical company engaged in developing, manufacturing, and marketing complex products for niche therapeutic areas. [1] NATCO has established its presence in all three business segments viz. finished dosage formulations (“FDF”), active pharmaceutical ingredients (“APIs”), Contract Manufacturing Business. [2]
